text:
amy (eng-platform): quick proposal — introducing a 'tiered cohort orchestrator' for model swaps. idea: instead of fixed microsteps, we define labeled cohorts with percentage targets + runtime safety envelopes (latency/cost/error budgets). looking for API/console feedback.

sam (eng-runtime): sounds promising. can you sketch the config shape? how do we express adaptive pauses? :eyes:

amy (eng-platform): yep. sketch below. key pieces: cohorts[], each cohort has target_percent, duration, min_samples, success_criteria (metric, window, threshold), and an optional 'attenuator' that reduces incoming traffic on transient failures. example: 
```yaml
strategy: tiered-cohort-orchestrator
cohorts:
  - name: tiny-cohort
    target_percent: 0.5
    duration: 10m
    min_samples: 200
    success_criteria:
      metric: p50_latency_ms
      window: 5m
      threshold: 200
    attenuator:
      backoff_on_error: true
      max_reduction_percent: 80
  - name: small-cohort
    target_percent: 5
    duration: 30m
    min_samples: 1000
    success_criteria:
      metric: error_rate
      window: 10m
      threshold: 0.01
  - name: rollout
    target_percent: 100
    duration: 2h
    min_samples: 10000
```

amy (eng-platform): policy also supports hooks: preflight-eval (run evals against shadow traffic) and telemetry-sampling (for detailed traces).

lucas (eng-sre): how does this interact with throttles/quotas? if dedicated pools hit capacity mid-cohort we could overcommit. want a guard that reduces cohort target when capacity < X.

amy (eng-platform): good call. add runtime-guards block that can reference capacity signals, quota headroom, or region health. plan: guard rules are boolean expressions referencing metrics (examples below). if guard trips, cohort enters 'attenuated' state and traffic is scaled down to cohort.target_percent * guard.reduction_factor.

sam (eng-runtime): example guard syntax?

amy (eng-platform): short example: 
```yaml
runtime_guards:
  - name: gpu_headroom_low
    when: "pool_gpu_headroom_pct < 15"
    reduction_factor: 0.2
    action: attenuate
  - name: region_error_spike
    when: "region_error_rate > 0.02 and p95_latency_ms > 1000"
    reduction_factor: 0.1
    action: pause_and_alert
```

kai (product-ux): console UX thoughts: show a preview curve (percent vs time) and overlay live telemetry bands (latency/error). allow a one-click 'fast-forward' for ops when auto checks pass and a single 'safe-rollback' button that snaps to previous model and reassigns cohorts. also add a compact summary card that lists cohorts and current state (waiting/active/attenuated/paused).

amy (eng-platform): love those. also want a small timeline control to tweak durations and reorder cohorts in the UI. would we expose the guard expressions to the UI or keep advanced editor only?

kai (product-ux): surface common guards with toggles in the main UI (e.g., capacity guard, error spike guard), and have an 'advanced' editor for boolean expressions. keep default safe presets.

lucas (eng-sre): telemetry: we need sampling rules for traces to avoid overload. suggest default: 100% of canary traffic gets basic metrics, 10% gets detailed traces, and 1% gets full trace+request logs. make these configurable per-cohort.

amy (eng-platform): we'll add telemetry_sampling per cohort, e.g. {metrics:1.0, traces:0.1, full_debug:0.01}. also support eval hooks that re-run golden prompt sets against canary outputs and fail if semantic drift > threshold.

sam (eng-runtime): what about A/B experiments mixing model variants (not strict canary). do we want the same schema?

amy (eng-platform): yes — cohorts can reference variants by id and weighting. strategy field will accept 'strict-rollout' vs 'ab-experiment'. ab-experiment cohorts pair >1 variant with internal split and evaluation hooks for per-variant quality metrics.

lucas (eng-sre): alerts: add a 'safety-hold' hook that will open a pager if error_rate increases by > X in rolling window OR if attenuation triggers > Y times in Z duration. otherwise just console alert.

amy (eng-platform): agree. default config will be conservative. open question for runtime: how aggressively should attenuator reduce traffic? current proposal caps reduction_factor so cohorts never drop below 0.1% unless explicitly configured. thoughts?

sam (eng-runtime): prefer floor of 0.5% for user-visible features, 0.1% ok for internal testing. lower floors complicate routing and attribution.

kai (product-ux): UI should warn if floor < 1% for public features and offer suggestions.

amy (eng-platform): sounds like consensus: default floor 0.5% for internal, 1% with UX warning for public. next steps: I'll open a PR with schema + server-side validators and a toy console mock. @sam @lucas @kai please review when I post. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployed draft schema to staging (env: staging, id: rollout-schema-v0.9)

sam (eng-runtime): thanks — will run some load tests against staging schema later today.

lucas (eng-sre): will add quota/capacity probes and a test that simulates attenuator flips.

amy (eng-platform): awesome. I'll ping with PR link and a short demo gif. appreciate the quick feedback! 

(kai added :eyes: reaction)
